title: AI Integration Maturity Framework
description: Evaluates AI-human interaction patterns across different integration maturity levels. Based on Luke Wroblewski's stages of AI integration from 'invisible enhancement' to AI-first interfaces.

thought_leader.name: Luke Wroblewski
thought_leader.key_insight: AI integration exists on a spectrum, each stage has fundamentally different interaction paradigms and evaluation criteria
thought_leader.implication: Evaluate based on the maturity stage, not one-size-fits-all criteria

paradigm_shift.from: Treating all AI as a single category with uniform evaluation
paradigm_shift.to: Recognizing distinct maturity stages with stage-appropriate evaluation criteria

maturity_stages.name: Invisible Enhancement
maturity_stages.description: AI improves existing experiences without users knowing AI is involved
characteristics: AI works entirely behind the scenes
No AI-specific UI elements or indicators
Users don't know AI is involved
Improvements feel like 'magic' or just good design

questions: Is the AI enhancement actually improving outcomes measurably?
Are there failure modes where users should know AI is involved?
Is there appropriate transparency for high-stakes decisions?
Does invisible AI create false mental models about the system?
what_to_look_for: No misleading users about system capabilities
anti_patterns: AI that degrades experience without user knowing why
Users attributing AI capabilities to their own judgment
No fallback when AI is unavailable

risks: Privacy concerns (what data is AI using?)

success_metrics.name: outcome_improvement_rate
success_metrics.description: How much better are outcomes with AI vs without

success_metrics.name: failure_transparency
success_metrics.target: Users can identify when AI has failed

maturity_stages.name: AI-Assisted
maturity_stages.description: AI provides suggestions that humans review and act on
characteristics: Clear AI suggestions visible to user
Human makes final decision on all actions
AI as advisor, not actor
Explicit accept/reject/modify flows

questions: Are AI suggestions clearly distinguished from system facts?
Is accepting/rejecting suggestions frictionless?
Does the system learn from accept/reject patterns?
Is suggestion confidence appropriately communicated?
what_to_look_for: Clear visual distinction for AI suggestions
anti_patterns: Same confidence display for all suggestions

success_metrics.name: suggestion_quality_over_time
success_metrics.measurement: Acceptance rate trend and user ratings

success_metrics.name: user_override_appropriateness
success_metrics.description: When users reject, are they right to?

maturity_stages.name: AI-Augmented
maturity_stages.description: AI handles routine work autonomously, humans handle exceptions and judgment calls
characteristics: AI takes autonomous action on routine items
Humans review exceptions and edge cases
Escalation mechanisms for uncertainty
Human-in-the-loop for anything requiring judgment
examples: Email triage with auto-response for routine

questions: Are routine/exception boundaries appropriate?
Is escalation to human smooth and timely?
Do humans have sufficient context when escalated to?
Is there an audit trail for AI decisions?
what_to_look_for: Clear criteria for what's routine vs exception
Smooth escalation flow with context handoff
anti_patterns: Too much escalation (AI adding no value)
No visibility into AI's autonomous decisions

risks: Skill atrophy (humans forget how to do routine work)

success_metrics.name: escalation_appropriateness
success_metrics.description: Escalated items actually need human judgment

success_metrics.name: human_context_sufficiency
success_metrics.description: Humans have what they need to decide
success_metrics.measurement: Human can decide without asking for more info

maturity_stages.name: AI-First
maturity_stages.description: AI is primary actor, humans provide oversight and strategic direction
characteristics: AI handles most interactions end-to-end
Human oversight via dashboards and controls
Strategic human input shapes AI behavior
Human intervention is exception, not norm

questions: Is human oversight meaningful or just theater?
Can humans intervene effectively when needed?
Does strategic human input actually shape AI behavior?
Are accountability and responsibility clear?
what_to_look_for: Oversight dashboards that surface what matters
Clear feedback loop from human direction to AI behavior
anti_patterns: Intervention mechanisms that don't work in practice

risks: Loss of human expertise (can't take over if needed)
Runaway automation (AI optimizes for wrong goal)

success_metrics.name: strategic_input_impact
success_metrics.description: Human direction measurably affects AI behavior

maturity_stages.name: Autonomous Partnership
maturity_stages.description: AI and human as true collaborators with complementary strengths
characteristics: Dynamic task allocation based on strengths
AI and human negotiate responsibilities
Mutual learning and adaptation
Emergent collaboration patterns

questions: Is task allocation optimizing for combined capability?
Does the partnership improve both AI and human over time?
Are collaboration patterns emergent and adaptive?
Is there genuine complementarity (not just task splitting)?
what_to_look_for: Dynamic handoffs based on who's best suited
anti_patterns: Static task allocation regardless of context

success_metrics.name: combined_capability_score
success_metrics.description: Partnership achieves more than either alone

step_1.name: Identify Current Maturity Stage
step_1.description: Determine which stage the AI feature is at
guidance: Map feature characteristics to stage definitions
Consider intended vs actual user interaction patterns
Identify the human role in the interaction

step_2.name: Apply Stage-Appropriate Criteria
step_2.description: Evaluate using criteria relevant to that stage
guidance: Don't apply Stage 5 criteria to Stage 2 features

step_3.name: Assess Progression Readiness
step_3.description: Evaluate if feature is ready for next maturity stage
guidance: Are current stage criteria well met?
Are there user needs for more autonomy?
Are safeguards in place for next stage?

step_4.name: Evaluate Stage-Specific Risks
step_4.description: Identify and assess risks unique to current stage
guidance: Each stage has characteristic failure modes
Assess likelihood and impact of each risk

step_5.name: Recommend Stage-Appropriate Improvements
guidance: Focus on maturity within stage, not jumping stages

when_to_use: Evaluating AI features at any maturity level
integration: Use with outcome-value-framework for value assessment
Use with ai-orchestration-patterns for Stage 3-5 features
